def choose_move(observation):
    # Defensive access for agent's current position
    agent_pos = observation.get("agent", {}).get("position", (0, 0))
    x, y = agent_pos

    # Check for resource collection
    if "resources" in observation:
        resources = observation.get("resources", [])
        if resources:
            # Find nearest resource
            min_dist = None
            target = None
            for res in resources:
                res_x, res_y = res.get("position", (x, y))
                dx = res_x - x
                dy = res_y - y
                dist = abs(dx) + abs(dy)
                if min_dist is None or dist < min_dist:
                    min_dist = dist
                    target = (res_x, res_y)
            if target:
                dx, dy = target[0] - x, target[1] - y
                # Clamp move to [-1,1]
                move_x = (dx > 0) - (dx < 0)
                move_y = (dy > 0) - (dy < 0)
                return [move_x, move_y]

    # Check for pursuit/evasion scenario
    if "agents" in observation:
        agents = observation.get("agents", [])
        for other in agents:
            if other != observation.get("agent_id") and "position" in other:
                other_pos = other.get("position")
                dx = other_pos[0] - x
                dy = other_pos[1] - y
                dist = abs(dx) + abs(dy)
                # Decide pursuit or evasion based on role
                role = observation.get("agent", {}).get("role", "")
                if role == "pursuer":
                    # Pursue nearest evader
                    move_x = (dx > 0) - (dx < 0)
                    move_y = (dy > 0) - (dy < 0)
                    return [move_x, move_y]
                elif role == "evader":
                    # Evade nearest pursuer
                    move_x = -(dx > 0) - (dx < 0)
                    move_y = -(dy > 0) - (dy < 0)
                    return [move_x, move_y]

    # Territory control fallback: random move towards center
    # For simplicity, move towards origin (0,0)
    dx = -x
    dy = -y
    move_x = (dx > 0) - (dx < 0)
    move_y = (dy > 0) - (dy < 0)
    return [move_x, move_y]
